children: The Middle East, North Africa and Türkiye (MENAT) region offers a pipeline of infrastructure projects worth $872 billion, reflecting robust investment potential and providing international and corporate investors with greater exposure to the region ahead of 2030, according to HSBC.

“This region has always demonstrated its ability to rebound quickly. Our commitment to the GCC region is steadfast. It will recover and continue growing on the back of alternative trade routes and businesses,” said Georges Elhedery, Group CEO of HSBC, during Future Forum 2026.

Investment to build resilient alternative logistics routes means that the Gulf region will recover from the impact of the Iran war. The Strait of Hormuz could become "redundant" in probably five years, he added.
The global investment bank has identified $872 billion in individual project packages within a wider $1.4 trillion planned and unawarded infrastructure pipeline.

The data shows that the value of planned but unawarded infrastructure projects and programmes increased by 54% between January 2023 and January 2026, from $792 billion to $1.22 trillion. Infrastructure planning activity has continued this year, with the pipeline increasing a further 15% to $1.4 trillion between January and October 2026, HSBC said in its latest infrastructure report.

Elhedery said capital would never be an issue for development in the GCC. “Capital is found very much internationally, and investors feel confident and are ready to participate in regional projects,” he said.
However, when it comes to tapping capital markets, the region must offer attractive structuring and pricing to draw international investors.

“Projects are more expensive than they used to be because of the conflict, but that is not just a Middle East story. The additional costs associated with energy and data security are not unique to the Middle East; they are a global phenomenon,” he said.
(Reporting by Seban Scaria; editing by Daniel Luiz)

title: HSBC Group CEO reaffirms GCC commitment, cites $872bln project pipeline
